headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or write overlap are documented, but A can emit API-driven workflow outputs that B could ingest if manually connected.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented: agent_a has REST/GRPC API surfaces and allowlisted egress, while agent_b has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, MCP, or network egress. Without a bridge, prompt injection from A into B is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts or files, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_b gains a shared workspace or message queue, reassess injection risk.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except through typed, validated fields.
Do not pipe raw A outputs into B prompts.
Add an allowlist for any future inter-agent message schema.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, shared OAuth principal, or any data class overlap that would flow from agent_a to agent_b. Agent_b cannot read files or use network egress, so there is no documented leakage path between them.
conditions: IF both agents are later mounted on the same workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is given file-reading or outbound network capability, reassess leakage.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in any shared intermediate artifact.
Review future mounts or volume shares before enabling them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability overlap is minimal and non-conflicting: agent_a can call APIs and has allowlisted egress, while agent_b cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use network egress. No shared mutable resource or locking issue is documented.
conditions: IF agent_b is later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess conflict.
IF agent_a is deployed with filesystem write privileges not shown here, reassess conflict.
mitigations: Do not grant both agents write access to the same repo or directory.
Document any future shared state with explicit locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce workflow outputs via APIs, but B is a document-processing agent with no documented action-taking authority or direct input bridge. Any cascade would require an external orchestrator to feed A's outputs into B, so the pathway is not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts treating A outputs as authoritative B inputs, cascade risk rises.
IF B is configured to execute downstream actions from parsed documents, reassess severity.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between A and B.
Require schema validation on A outputs before B consumes them.
Log and review any A-to-B handoff for provenance.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or PHI/PII handling mismatch is documented. Agent_a touches artifacts and parameters only, and agent_b lists no data classes touched, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent, reassess compliance.
IF either agent is assigned a jurisdiction-specific workload, reassess residency and retention controls.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Record retention and residency requirements for any regulated workload.
Recheck vendor controls before handling sensitive data.
